lesson.title: Prohibition and classification capstone
lesson.summary: Combine biometric-practice analysis with prohibition, classification, timing and evidence in a bounded final assessment.

prerequisites.reason: The final case requires a classification conclusion after prohibition screening.
The final case includes the harmful-decision prohibition tests.
The synthesis includes untargeted scraping for a facial-recognition database.
The synthesis includes the medical/safety boundary of the emotion prohibition.
The synthesis includes the categorisation prohibition and its stated boundary.
The final case includes the distinct tests and date for the added synthetic-media prohibitions.
The synthesis includes a remote-identification authorisation refusal.

blocks: For **biometric-practice synthesis**, identify the function before the legal label: identity verification, remote identification, categorisation or emotion inference. Then establish data, purpose, actor, setting and timing.

Fictional Northbridge bundle contains workplace facial emotion scoring, post-event identification and a missing-person real-time station search. Shared camera hardware does not make their intended functions or prohibition tests identical.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2–6, 5(1a)–(8), 6(3)–(4), 113; Annexes I–III

blocks: The workplace emotion function needs Article 5(1)(f)'s elements and medical/safety boundary; do not substitute a wellbeing label. The real-time search needs a listed strictly necessary objective plus paragraphs 2–3 and applicable national rules.

The post-event function has a different real-time fact, but may remain listed under Annex III and subject to other law. A narrowly permitted use remains subject to independent classification, privacy and decision requirements.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2–6, 5(1a)–(8), 6(3)–(4), 113; Annexes I–III

blocks: A **final prohibition and classification assessment** begins with source version, scope, AI-system/actor definitions, intended purpose and evidence. Apply each relevant prohibition with its complete elements. Then test the appropriate Annex I or Annex III classification route.

For an Annex III exception, retain the no-significant-harm/material-influence gateway, a qualifying condition and the profiling override. Document any exemption assessment and registration obligations. Stipulated sector facts are case assumptions, not an unsourced real-world product classification.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2–6, 5(1a)–(8), 6(3)–(4), 113; Annexes I–III

blocks: Finish with dates and unresolved questions. In this baseline, the new synthetic-media points apply on 2 December 2026; Annex III high-risk obligations have a 2 December 2027 date and Annex I a 2 August 2028 date under Article 113's specified section rules. Other applicable rules have their own dates.

A useful handoff identifies the conclusion, exact provision, facts supporting each element, remaining evidence, responsible reviewer and applicable date. This English first release teaches foundations, Article 6 and Article 5; full downstream obligations and the dedicated Article 50 block remain follow-on teaching.

questions.prompt: Three functions share a camera: emotion scoring, post-event identification and real-time missing-person search. What is the sound first step?

options.blocks: Separate intended functions, settings and relevant tests
options.reason: Different functions and facts engage different definitions and conditions.

options.blocks: Treat all three as automatically permitted identity verification
options.reason: The bundle contains materially different functions.

options.blocks: Assign one result from the camera brand
options.reason: Brand does not establish the legal function or purpose.
